Done. The environment had no board repo, so I built a faithful reproduction, implemented the fix, verified it end-to-end, and wrote the self-contained solution.

## Deliverables

- **`/workspace/solution.md`** — title, root-cause analysis, exact fix, verification
- **`/workspace/scripts/board_recover.py`** — auto-detects the wiping commit, merges last-good + current, dedupes by `id` keeping last occurrence, optional P1 re-file
- **`/workspace/scripts/board_guard.py`** — pre-commit net-delete abort (`>3` removed ids)

## What was proven

1. **Wipe reproduced exactly** — bad write yielded `1 insertion(+), 56 deletions(-)`, matching the reported commit.
2. **Recovery verified** — dry-run/apply restored all 56 rows + the 1 live new row, deduped by id (last=live), and re-filed the wipe as a P1 row; all ids unique (58 rows).
3. **Guard verified** — blocked the stale-snapshot wipe (`exit=1`), allowed an append-only write (`exit=0`), and rejected a wipe commit *through an installed git pre-commit hook* (`git commit exit=1`).
4. **Manual one-liner verified** — the pure-git recovery path (last-occurrence-wins) produces the correct deduped output.

Key detail: last-occurrence-wins is what resolves re-filed ids, so the live row from the bad commit overwrites any stale copy rather than being discarded.

signatures.description: qa-foreman board writer deleted all 56 rows of a JSONL board (commit claimed 1 new, 0 deduped but diff showed 56 deletions): writer rewrote tasks.jsonl from an empty/stale snapshot instead of read-modify-append. Recovery: git log --oneline to find last-good commit, git show <last-good>:path/to/tasks.jsonl, dedupe by id keeping LAST occurrence (re-filed ids: last=live), rewrite file, re-file wipe as a P1 task. Prevention to demand from writer owners: append-only writes + net-delete abort (>3 removed rows = refuse to commit).
